study_name.evidence_quote: The Kailuan study is a prospective cohort study focusing on the Kailuan community

target_condition.evidence_quote: Hypertension is one of the most prevalent cardiovascular diseases worldwide
target_condition.notes: Study investigates pre-hypertension and primary hypertension

country.evidence_quote: a large modern city in northern China

location.evidence_quote: Tangshan, a large modern city in northern China

body_site.evidence_quote: shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from a cohort of 196

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: received antibiotics or probiotics within the last 8 weeks

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Bacterial DNA was extracted using TIANGEN kit

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: All samples were paired-end sequenced on the Illumina platform
sequencing_platform.notes: Illumina platform used; specific HiSeq model inferred from read specs (125-bp paired-end reads)

sex.evidence_quote: Male GF mice at 8–10 weeks were divided into groups
sex.notes: From transplantation experiment; human cohort sex distribution not explicitly stated per sample

subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers reported in paper; cohort-level data only

sample_id.notes: No individual sample identifiers reported in paper; aggregated analyses only

subcohort.notes: Participants stratified by condition (control, pre-hypertension, hypertension) but no subcohort identifier given

body_site_details.notes: Fecal samples collected but no more specific anatomical subsite specified

days_from_first_collection.notes: Appears to be cross-sectional study without longitudinal follow-up reported

lifestyle.notes: Participants from modern urban setting (employees) but specific lifestyle category not classified

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; study focused on gut microbiota and hypertension, not periodontal disease

westernized.evidence_quote: employees of the Kailuan Group Corporation, a large modern city
westernized.notes: Participants from modern urban setting and employed workforce; inferred as westernized

probing_pocket_depth_value.notes: Not applicable; study did not measure probing pocket depth

age.notes: Age data not reported in main text or tables; no per-sample age provided

family_role.notes: Not applicable; no family-based relationships reported

ncbi_accession.notes: No NCBI SRA/ENA accessions mentioned in paper text

control.notes: Paper reports aggregated cohort-level data for three groups (control n=41, pre-hypertension n=56, hypertension n=99) without sample-level case/control assignment

zigosity.notes: Twin zygosity not applicable; study involves unrelated cohort members.

antibiotics_current_use.section: Methods — Study cohort and patient characteristics
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Study excluded participants who received antibiotics within 8 weeks, indicating no current antibiotic use in the cohort.

bmi.notes: BMI not reported in Results or Tables; mentioned only in correlation analysis where no regular BMI pattern emerged.

dietary_restriction.notes: No specific dietary restrictions reported for participants.

disease.evidence_quote: a cohort of 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pre-hypertension, 99 individuals with primary hypertension
disease.notes: Three disease/condition groups used in study design.

value: Hypertension (blood pressure classified per clinical guidelines)

Pre-hypertension (pHTN): 125 mmHg < SBP ≤ 139 mmHg, or 80 mmHg < DBP ≤ 89 mmHg

disease_details.evidence_quote: It was composed of 41 healthy controls (SBP ≤125 mmHg, or DBP ≤80 mmHg), 56 pHTNs (125 mmHg < SBP ≤ 139 mmHg, or 80 mmHg < DBP ≤ 89 mmHg), 99 patients of HTN (140 mmHg ≤ SBP, or 90 mmHg ≤ DBP).
disease_details.section: Methods — Study cohort and patient characteristics
disease_details.notes: Classification based on systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) according to Internal Guidelines for HTN.

disease_response_orr.notes: Not applicable; study design does not measure treatment response in hypertensive patients.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable; hypertension microbiome study not focused on cancer or progression-free survival.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Not applicable; no PFS follow-up reported.

disease_response_recist.notes: Not applicable; RECIST criteria used for solid tumors, not hypertension.

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: Stool samples freshly collected from each participant were immediately frozen at −20 °C and transported to the laboratory with ice pack.
feces_phenotype.section: Methods — Stool sample collection and DNA extraction
feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples analyzed via shotgun metagenomic sequencing and 16S rRNA sequencing for microbiota characterization.

fmt_id.notes: Study-specific identifiers not provided for FMT participants; donors and recipients noted only by group (control or HTN).

fmt_role.evidence_quote: fecal bacteria from hypertensive patients were transplanted to GF mice. The donors for microbiota transplantation consisted of two patients of HTN and one normotensive control.
fmt_role.section: Results — High BP is transferrable by fecal transplant
fmt_role.notes: Human donors (n=3: 2 HTN patients, 1 control); recipient mice (n=15 total: 5 control, 10 HTN).

hla.notes: HLA typing not reported in study.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Study includes adults from Kailuan Corporation cohort; neonatal data not applicable.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Study population is adults; delivery mode not reported.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Study population is adults; infant feeding data not applicable or reported.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Study population is adults; gestational age not applicable.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Study population is adults; preterm birth not applicable.

obgyn_birth_control.notes: Oral contraceptive use not reported; study notes gender ratio discrepant among groups but does not analyze contraceptive effects.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Menopausal status not reported; gender ratio noted as discrepant but not analyzed.

smoker.evidence_quote: Patients suffering from cancer, heart failure, renal failure, smoking, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and chronic inflammatory disease were all excluded.
smoker.section: Methods — Study cohort and patient characteristics
smoker.notes: Smoking was an exclusion criterion; all study participants are non-smokers.

treatment.evidence_quote: All the subjects in the hypertension group were newly diagnosed hypertensive patients prior to antihypertensive treatment. Drugs including statins, aspirin, insulin, metformin, nifedipine, and metoprolol were not used on the patients.
treatment.section: Results — GM diversity and enterotype in pHTN and HTN
treatment.notes: Study enrolled treatment-naive hypertensive patients and excluded those on specific medications to avoid confounding microbiome effects.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; study focuses on hypertension, not cancer.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Not applicable; hypertension study does not employ TNM staging.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Genera such as Prevotella and Klebsiella were overrepresented in individuals with pHTN or HTN. Faecalibacterium, Oscillibacter, Roseburia, Bifidobacterium, Coprococcus, and Butyrivibrio declined in pHTN and HTN patients.
biomarker_name.section: Results — pHTN and HTN-associated genera in GM
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple bacterial genera and metabolites identified as biomarkers for hypertension and pre-hypertension status.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Relative abundance of gut microbes was calculated by summing the abundance of genes. Serum samples were subjected to LC/MS analysis.
biomarker_unit.section: Methods — pHTN and HTN-associated genera in GM; Metabonomics analysis
biomarker_unit.notes: Units inferred from measurement methodology; bacterial abundances are relative, metabolites quantified via LC/MS.

feces_phenotype_value.section: Abstract; Results — GM diversity and enterotype
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes characterized through metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of stool samples.

value: Cohort study from Kailuan Group Corporation, Tangshan, China
196 Chinese individuals: 41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertension subjects, 99 primary hypertension patients
Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples; 1211 Gb total reads generated
Fecal microbiota transplantation from hypertensive patients to germ-free mice
Blood pressure measured at 10 weeks post-transplantation using tail-cuff method
HTN mice showed significantly higher SBP (P=0.018), DBP (P=0.019), MBP (P=0.014)
Random forest classifier achieved AUC 0.91 for control vs HTN; AUC 0.89 for control vs pre-hypertension
Validation cohort from type 2 diabetes study: 3 HTN and 3 normotensive controls
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 196 Chinese individuals. 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pHTN, 99 patients with primary HTN. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples. Fecal microbiota transplantation from hypertensive human donors to germ-free mice.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Additional study design and results details included for comprehensive metadata documentation.

host_species.evidence_quote: 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pHTN, 99 patients with primary HTN. All the subjects were from a cohort study among employees of the Kailuan Group Corporation.
host_species.section: Methods — Study cohort and patient characteristics
host_species.notes: Human participants explicitly stated throughout methods and results; also includes germ-free C57BL/6L mice as experimental animal model.
